source.library: ATNI plan-assessor public plan library: national discovery corpus ledger 007 and the library campaign inventory (documents found on public websites or their Wayback copies)
source.tribes: ATNI-listed Tribes: the 55 federally recognized Tribes on a captured ATNI directory page, plus listed Tribes outside the federal register list that hold documents in the library; listed Tribes outside that list that hold no documents in the library are not shown (Chinook Tribe, Snohomish Tribe, Steilacoom Tribe)
source.extraction: Text from the library campaign's extraction where finished (1099 of 1676 library records extracted when this was built), else the PDF's own text layer; no OCR was run for this analysis

method.summary: Each Tribe's public planning documents in the library were searched page by page for 13 energy types. Passages around the matches were read by a calibrated judgment model (TypeSafe Jev), which answered three questions per type: whether the passage describes the Tribe's own energy work, how far that work has progressed, and whether it was found unsuitable. Code then ranked the types by the most advanced stage found, with a small bonus for support in several documents. A second model pass checked each ranked claim against its cited excerpts; a claim the excerpts did not support was re-checked one stage lower, and dropped if no stage held. Fossil fuel backup (diesel generators, propane, natural gas) and transmission are not ranked.
method.judgment_model: TypeSafe Jev (jev-1.14.0); stage read as the most probable level

verification.rule: second Jev pass per claim over its excerpts with their document, year and page: >= 0.7 verified, 0.3 to 0.7 needs review, below 0.3 dropped and re-checked one stage lower
verification.spot_check: 15 published claims were checked by hand against their cited pages: 14 agreed with the claimed stage; 1 cited another Tribe's measure in a plan shared by several Tribes and was withheld.

caveats: This is a machine-assisted reading of public planning documents. It is not the Tribe's own assessment, and it is not an endorsement of any project.
Each Tribe is the authority on its own plans and priorities.
Plans may be outdated, and newer plans may exist that the library does not hold.
The attribution of documents to Tribes comes from the library and may be imperfect.
ATNI listing comes from a capture of ATNI's directory page and records a listing, not membership certification.
Some documents still await text extraction, so a Tribe's entry may change when they are read.
A Tribe can ask ATNI to correct or remove its entry.
